notes: DNA pipelines need DNA libraries. A cohort whose lineage holds only RNA-seq libraries (LibrarySource TRANSCRIPTOMIC, LibraryStrategy RNA-Seq) cannot run sarek, even when the question asks about variants; rnavar is the RNA route.

sarek.answers: Which germline SNVs, indels and structural variants does each sample carry, and, for a tumour with its matched normal, which somatic mutations and copy-number changes are in the tumour?
sarek.assumes_prep: Short-read Illumina DNA libraries: whole genome, whole exome or targeted capture.
sarek.input_you_must_have: FASTQ per sample. For somatic calling, a tumour and a matched normal from the same patient, both linked to that patient in NExtSEEK. For exome or capture, the kit's target-region BED on the cluster.
sarek.species_constraint: HUMAN on Luria today: only the GATK GRCh38 bundle is staged. Another species needs its own references staged first.

rnavar.differs_by: sarek calls variants from DNA libraries. rnavar calls them from RNA-seq reads, so it sees only expressed transcripts.
rnavar.ask_user: Are these DNA libraries (genome, exome, panel) or RNA-seq?

hlatyping.differs_by: sarek reports variants genome-wide. hlatyping resolves HLA alleles against a specialist reference; sarek does not type HLA.

methylseq.differs_by: methylseq reads bisulfite or enzymatically converted libraries for methylation; sarek on those reads would call conversions as mutations.
methylseq.ask_user: Were these libraries bisulfite or EM-seq converted?

atacseq.answers: Where is chromatin open in each sample, how consistent are the open regions between replicates, and which regions open or close between conditions?
atacseq.assumes_prep: ATAC-seq: Tn5 transposase tagmentation of native chromatin, short-read Illumina, single- or paired-end.
atacseq.input_you_must_have: Gzipped FASTQ per sample with a replicate number. Two or more conditions for differential accessibility. A reference genome with an annotation.
atacseq.species_constraint: No ATAC references are staged on Luria yet: the launch is built with the iGenomes reference for the species and the reply must say references need staging before it can run.

chipseq.differs_by: chipseq maps where one protein or histone mark binds, using an antibody and usually an input control; atacseq maps open chromatin with no antibody.
chipseq.ask_user: Was an antibody used (ChIP), or is this transposase accessibility (ATAC)?

rnaseq.differs_by: rnaseq measures transcripts; atacseq measures which DNA is accessible. ATAC libraries are genomic DNA.

chipseq.answers: Where does a protein or histone mark bind across the genome in each sample, compared with its input control where one exists, and how consistent are the peaks between replicates?
chipseq.assumes_prep: ChIP-seq: chromatin immunoprecipitation with an antibody, short-read Illumina, single- or paired-end. An input (or IgG) control library for each IP is usual but optional. CUT&RUN and CUT&Tag tether an enzyme to the antibody, start from far fewer cells and usually have no input control; they are not ChIP-seq and NExtSEEK cannot launch them yet. When the metadata does not say which assay it is, ask the user: ChIP-seq with an input control, or CUT&RUN / CUT&Tag?
chipseq.input_you_must_have: Gzipped FASTQ per sample, with replicates numbered from 1 within each experimental group. The antibody name for each IP sample (required for any sample that has a control) and, where a control exists, which sample is its control and which replicate of it. A reference genome with an annotation.
chipseq.species_constraint: No ChIP references are staged on Luria yet: the launch is built with the iGenomes reference for the species and the reply must say references need staging before it can run.

atacseq.differs_by: atacseq maps open chromatin by transposase; chipseq maps antibody-bound sites, against an input control where one exists.
atacseq.ask_user: Was an antibody used (ChIP), or is this transposase accessibility (ATAC)?

methylseq.answers: How methylated is each cytosine (CpG and, where covered, non-CpG) in each sample, from bisulfite or enzymatic conversion sequencing?
methylseq.assumes_prep: Whole-genome bisulfite (WGBS), reduced-representation bisulfite (RRBS), enzymatic methyl conversion (EM-seq) or PBAT libraries, short-read Illumina, single- or paired-end. TAPS runs are not offered until the launch template supports methylseq's `--taps` with bwamem.
methylseq.input_you_must_have: Gzipped FASTQ per sample, and which conversion and library type was used (WGBS, RRBS, EM-seq, PBAT), because the trimming and the aligner settings depend on it.
methylseq.species_constraint: No methylation references (a bisulfite-converted index) are staged on Luria yet: the launch is built with the iGenomes reference for the species and the reply must say references need staging before it can run.

sarek.differs_by: sarek calls variants from ordinary DNA reads. Bisulfite or enzymatically converted reads turn unmethylated C into T, so sarek would call those as mutations; they go to methylseq only.
sarek.ask_user: Were these libraries bisulfite or EM-seq converted?

rnaseq.differs_by: methylseq reads converted genomic DNA and reports cytosine methylation; rnaseq reads transcripts and reports expression. A question about how methylation relates to expression needs both runs, one on each kind of library.
rnaseq.ask_user: Do you want the methylation of these DNA libraries, or the expression of RNA libraries?
